body.heading: Shrink the starting line
paragraphs: Big plans often fail at the very first step. Reading a whole book feels heavy; reading for two minutes feels almost too easy to skip. That is exactly the point — make the start so small that saying no feels sillier than starting.

Pick the smallest honest version of what you want to do: two minutes of stretching, one page of notes, a single paragraph of writing. You are not cheating. You are building the doorway, and doorways are what habits walk through.

body.heading: Let two minutes grow on their own
paragraphs: Most days, once you have started, continuing feels natural and the two minutes quietly become ten. Some days they will not, and that is fine too. The two minutes still count, because the habit you are really training is showing up.
Keep the two-minute version as your official minimum even as the habit grows. On busy or tired days it protects the streak, and a protected streak is much easier to restart than a broken one.

takeaway: Make the start tiny, and let momentum do the rest.
